Container.Name: VidCleaner
Container.Overview:
Mutes profanity in the audio of movies and TV episodes managed by Sonarr/Radarr and played through Jellyfin. Adds a "Clean" audio track as the new default and keeps the original track and an untouched backup of the source file, so every change is reversible.
Speech is located locally on the CPU (faster-whisper + whisperX) and muted with ffmpeg; no cloud service and no GPU. Existing subtitles narrow the search to about 5% of an episode's runtime, which is what makes CPU-only recognition practical. New downloads are processed automatically via Sonarr/Radarr webhooks, and a web UI shows every word that was removed with a five-second before/after clip so a false positive can be whitelisted and the file reprocessed.
IMPORTANT: /media must be the SAME path Sonarr, Radarr and Jellyfin use, and PUID/PGID must match whoever owns that share -- otherwise the swap cannot write. Keep /backups on the media share so swaps are same-filesystem renames, and put /work on a cache pool. The first job downloads a speech model (~1.5 GB) into /config, so it is much slower than the ones after it.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Database, settings, logs and downloaded STT models

Config.Name: Media
Config.Description: Your library. MUST be the same path Sonarr/Radarr/Jellyfin use.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Original files kept until purged. Keep it on the media share so swaps are same-filesystem renames.

Config.Name: Work
Config.Description: Scratch space for in-progress jobs. Put this on an SSD/cache pool.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id that owns the media share

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id that owns the media share

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: File mode mask for everything VidCleaner writes. 0002 keeps the group bit so the arrs can still manage the files.

Config.Name: OMP_NUM_THREADS
Config.Description: Threads for speech-to-text. Leave blank for CPU cores minus 2. Must be set here rather than in the web UI, because the threading library reads it once at start-up.

Config.Name: Role
Config.Description: all | api | worker — split only for multi-host setups
